cases.title: The Golden Butterfly
objectives: Investigate the Moller Residence and Interview Michelle Moller and Hugo Moller
Speak to Moller’s Neighbour and Apprehend Hugo Moller
Investigate High School and Apprehend the Molester
Return to Central Station and Interview Hugo Moller and Eli Rooney

blocks.title: Briefing
paragraphs: The case opens with yet another gruesome attack. A woman steps out of a car in a parking lot and drops her keys. As she bends to get them, she is bludgeoned by a man wearing a shirt and vest with a tire iron in hand.

The next day, Rusty takes the call about the murder. A woman has been killed and dumped in the grass at the end of Hill Street. Phelps points out that it is similar to the Henry case, but Galloway says the first rule of being a detective is to never assume anything until you’ve seen the evidence. Go view the evidence then!

blocks.title: Crime Scene
paragraphs: Arrive at the scene and you are once again met by reporters looking for a story to link the murder with the previous case, and the Black Dahlia case. Head to the scene and you’ll be shown to the Coroner by uniformed police. Carruthers notes that the murder has a similar M.O. to the previous case, left on display and stomped. Examine the body.
First examine the head, revealing a rope pattern on the woman’s neck. Carruthers notes that the pattern is very distinctive, and he’ll run tests at the lab and get back to you.

Then examine the right hand, where you find another mark, which Carruthers suggests may be from a wristwatch being torn off. On the left hand you get the familiar mark of a ring being removed by force, adding Missing Jewelry to your clues. Examine her chest to get the clue for small men’s footprints.

Examine the surrounding area. An evidence marker has her handbag next to it, with a wad of cash inside. Not robbery then. Cole pulls out a nametag giving you an ID on the victim, Deidre Moller. Phelps asks Gonzales (the uniformed officer) to run the name through R&I.

An evidence marker has the small men’s footprints again, which will be added to your clues if you didn’t search the torso of the victim. Phelps asks if the stomping from Henry’s murder was leaked to the press, which it was. If somebody wanted to copy the Henry killing, they wouldn’t need to look far.

After this, Gonzales returns to tell you that Deidre Moller was reported missing by her husband, Hugo, this morning. This adds the Moller residence to your locations, and gives you your next port of call.

blocks.title: Moller Residence

clues.name: Missing Watch and Rings (updates missing jewelry)

paragraphs: Knock on the door to trigger a quick scene. You are greeted by 15 year old daughter of Deidre Moller, Michelle. She invites the officers inside, then Phelps asks her to sit while he searches the area.

Enter the hallway, turn right and head for the master bedroom. Inside, you’ll find the size 8 workboots on the floor. Now examine the top of the dresser and you’ll find an empty Lady Elgin watch case, and an empty ring case. Examine both to get the clue updated.
Now head back to the living room and break the bad news to Michelle. She takes it rather well, and agrees to be questioned.

blocks.title: Michelle Moller

topics.instruction: Last Contact with Victim: Bad Cop
topics.response: Michelle says she last saw her mother the previous afternoon, before the girl was attended a dance at her school. When her mother didn’t show to pick her up, her father came instead. She gives a slight wince and can’t look at you, so she’s holding something back. Go Bad Cop on her, and she will admit that she called home repeatedly, with no answer, before her father eventually picked up the phone and came immediately to get her. This provides you with Husband’s Alibi.

topics.instruction: Missing Watch a Rings: Good Cop
topics.response: Phelps asks about the jewelry. Michelle recalls that her mother had a ring and watch, but says she didn’t pay much attention. She holds your gaze, so believe her and she’ll give details on the rings and watch, before saying the watch was a make-up present from her father to Deidre after a fight.

topics.instruction: State of Parents’ Marriage: Bad Cop
topics.response: When Phelps asks if her parents are happily married, she replies that they are, but appears defensive. Select Bad Cop and she says that her father hit her mother once, but bought her a butterfly brooch to make up for it.

paragraphs: After the interview, Phelps claims that the girl has been very brave, and Hugo Moller enters the house. He sends his daughter away, then is shocked by the new of Deidre. He sits and agrees to questioning.

blocks.title: Hugo Moller

topics.instruction: Footprints at Crime Scene: Accuse - Size 8 workboots
topics.response: Phelps asks what size shoe Hugo wears, to which he replies nines. Why has he got 8s in his bedroom then? Call his bluff and bring up the boots you found, and he replies that he often gets teased for his small feet.

Hugo confirms that he filed a missing person report for his wife that morning. He says she left home at 9.30PM and never arrived to pick their daughter up. He seems pretty honest, but he’s very nervous, so he’s clearly holding something back. Go with Bad Cop and Phelps asks if Deidre often went to any bars by herself. Moller gets pretty cross at the insinuation. He says they argued about who was picking Michelle up from the dance.

topics.instruction: Alibi for Hugo Moller: Accuse - Husband’s Alibi
topics.response: Phelps asks if Hugo stayed at home all night, which he says he did. However, if you correctly branched everything in the Michelle interview, you know he wasn’t answering his phone all night, so call him out with the husband’s alibi clue, and he admits to going for a drive to relax. Another topic appears in your questioning.

topics.instruction: History of Violence: Accuse - Butterfly Brooch
topics.response: Phelps describes the brutality of Deidre’s murder and points out that Hugo has a history of being violent towards his wife. Hugo denies it, but you know of an object used as a payoff for a previous attack. Bring up the butterfly brooch, and Hugo denies that he is a violent man who is feared by his wife and daughter.

paragraphs: Phelps tells Hugo to report to Central station himself for questioning, even though Rusty wants to drag the man away in cuffs. That’s not fair on the daughter, but Phelps does warn Hugo not to run.

Heading outside, you’ll have a quick conversation with Rusty, then the neighbour calls you over. She reports that the Mollers had a very loud argument the night before, and that she saw Hugo Moller burning something in his incinerator that morning. She then spots Hugo at the incinerator again, and you take off after him.

blocks.title: Moller Residence (After the Chase)
paragraphs: Inspect the incinerator to see what Hugo wanted to burn. You’ll find a blooded shoe, and when you turn it over, it is size 8. Amazing how these coincidences happen isn’t it? Hugo says he can explain, but you haul him off in the paddy wagon.

Head to the game well to get the address for Belmont High School, and then head back to your car. As you enter, you get a call from central that Carruthers has his coroner’s report for you, so swing around the morgue.

blocks.title: Central Morgue
paragraphs: Travel to the Central Morgue. Enter through the night entrance and go right to enter the examination room to trigger a cutscene.

Phelps first asks if the blood found on the shoes can be matched to the victim's blood. Carruthers then confirms that Strangulation was the cause of death, and shows you the samples on the desk. Choose the bottom one, and hold it against the picture to match the rope to the wound, and Rusty and Carruthers tell you that the rope is most commonly used on boats as mooring lines, but also used as bellrope in churches. Carruthers says he found no trace of sexual assault.
Now examine the shoeprint molds to the right of the rope samples. They are size 8 shoe prints, and they are also very similar to the prints in the Celine Henry case.
Exit the morgue, and you’ll get a call from KGPL, which will tell you that Deidre Moller’s car has been found on the car park at Belmont High school. Head there now.

blocks.title: Belmont High School
paragraphs: Chat to the school janitor. He says he saw somebody park the car there at 1AM the previous morning. He mentions some recent problems with a child molester, but he doesn’t know if it is the same guy. Before he says anymore, he spots the child molester.

Chase the molester through the first gap in the bleachers on your right, then sprint across the playing field to the far bleachers. Head around them and up the stairs onto the street level. Follow him down an alley way and then through people’s back yards as he tries to cut through them to get away.

After you get the guy, you drag him back to the car park and he gives his name as Eli Rooney. Rooney says he knows nothing of the woman who was killed, but when he turns his pockets out, he has a very familiar butterfly brooch on his person. He claims he found it in the parking lot.
After Rooney is hauled away, open the truck of Moller’s car to find the rest of the clues. Examine the rope, bloody tire iron and the overalls, which have the initials H.M on. Hugo Moller?
Use the game well nearby to set up the two suspects in interview rooms, then head back to Central Station.

blocks.title: Central Station
paragraphs: You’ll be conducting both interviews here. By interviewing Moller first, you don’t have to swap between the two or do too much cross referencing, so head for interview room 2 first.

blocks.title: Hugo Moller

topics.response: When Phelps asks why Moller was burning the shoes, he replies that it was because he knew you wouldn’t believe what he said. It’s a straightforward and honest answer, so believe him and he will say the blood is from a skinned rabbit. If it was false, then the coroner would be able to prove it wrong anyway.

topics.instruction: Access to Braided Rope: Bad Cop
topics.response: Phelps asks how much Hugo knows about rope. He claims that he was a scout, and then learned a bit more in the army, but other than that, nothing more than an average fellow. Choosing Bad Cop will make Phelps push about the strangulation. Moller admits he learnt a lot of ways to strangle someone in the army. If he had to choose a rope to use, he’d choose triple braid rope, the same that was used to kill Deidre. That’s a strange admission if Hugo knew the rope that killed his wife.

topics.instruction: Access to Tire Iron: Accuse - Bloody Tire Iron
topics.response: Phelps points out that Deidre was beaten by a tire iron, which would be appropriate tool for a mechanic to use. Hugo denies knowledge of the tire iron, but his eyes turn shifty. Bring up the bloody tire iron you found in Deidre’s car and he admits that he drives a Chrysler Airflow, which is the same make as the tire iron that killed his wife.

Phelps tells Hugo that they recovered his wife’s vehicle, then asks where he keeps his work clothes. Hugo says he keeps them in his locker, but you know that they were in his wife’s car. Bring up the overalls, and Hugo continues to deny that they could be his.

paragraphs: This concludes Hugo Moller’s investigation. You get the option to leave or charge the suspect. Leave, as you still need to interview Rooney.

blocks.title: Eli Rooney

topics.instruction: Footprints at the Crime Scene: Bad Cop
topics.response: Phelps asks what shoes Eli wears. He replies whatever he can get his hands on, and that these are 11s. But he’s a small guy, and 11s would bury his feet. Choose Bad Cop, and he’ll say he might just wear an 8. Phelps asks why he harms children, and he seems to suggest it is to do with his own abused childhood.

Phelps asks where Rooney works. He says he used to work in San Pedro but was looking for something new. He’s not giving you much to work with, and seems guarded, so pick Bad Cop him again and you’ll be told that his ex-employer was Hennessy Marines, which would match the initials on the overalls. He also admits that he was given some green overalls, which would also match.

topics.instruction: Access to Braided Rope: Good Cop
topics.response: Phelps asks if he ever ties up his victims, which he admits to. He says he has no particular preference as to the rope. Believe him, and Rooney goes on to say if you use triple braid, it stays tied no matter what.

topics.instruction: Motive for Moller Murder: Bad Cop
topics.response: Phelps suggests that Rooney killed Moller for her jewelry, which he flat out denies, which is a different reaction to what you have been getting. Pick Bad Cop, and he tells his story. He says he saw the car pull into the car park the previous night. A man got out of the car, changed his clothes and put the overalls in the trunk, before dropping the brooch. Rooney then picked up the brooch.

paragraphs: Eli Rooney is scum, and people like him are hated by the police. He shows signs of being battered recently. Looks like they’ve not been easy on him.
You are again given the choice to charge or leave. So hit charge and wrap up the case. Plus, you’re getting a child abuser off the streets, which can only be a good thing.

cases.title: The Silk Stocking Murder
objectives: Investigate Antonia’s Room and Interview Mrs Lapent
Investigate Maldonado Residence and Canvass Neighbours
Investigate El Dorado Bar and Interview Diego Aguilar
Investigate Just Picked Fruit Market and Interview Clem Feeney

blocks.title: Briefing
paragraphs: This case starts in the Mirror Press Diner, a cop hideout down the road from Central Station. Phelps, Galloway and Donnelly meet over breakfast, and you get given a new case, another woman murdered and left on show. Phelps again comments that it is similar to the previous two cases, and it is, but Rusty and Donnelly ignore Phelps’ concerns, and you’re sent on your way.

blocks.title: Downtown Crime Scene
paragraphs: This is a pretty big investigation, so follow carefully to get all of the clues in this area. Remember, if you’ve missed one, the clue music will continue playing.
Approach the coroner, who says the cause of death is apparent, and that he waited for you before examining further. Head over to the body.

Start by examining the head. Phelps points out that there was great force applied to her neck, based on the deep lacerations there. On her torso, you will find another lipstick message, which says “Kiss the Blood B.D”

Examine the left hand to find that another ring has been torn from the finger. Then examine the other hand to find half of a library card, which tells you the victim’s first name, Antonia, and that she was 21 years old.

The investigators talk about the similarities between this case, the previous 2, and the Black Dahlia murder. Carruthers adds that the shoe prints are another similarity, as is the color of the lipstick applied to the victim.

Search the rest of the scene. An evidence marker has the Bloodied Stocking. Then notice the blood smeared across the street. Follow it to find a blue Ladies Hat. When you look at it, you find the name Antonia inside.

The blood trail continues up the alley, past the squad car. Follow it until you reach the trash can next to a blood smear on the wall. Inside, you’ll find a bloody ladies shoe, which gives you the Personal Effects clue.
Keep following the blood to the water pipe, and you’ll find a key hanging on a piece of string. Examine it, and you’ll see it belongs to an apartment 5 of whichever building it is from.

Pick up the blood trail again, and follow it until you find a piece of paper on the ground. Unfold it, and there is a dot pattern on it. Phelps suggests that it is a code for something. It also looks like this trail is left deliberately.
The next blood splash is on the wall next to the fire escape ladder. Rusty gazes up at the roof as a clue as to where to go next. Head up the ladder and reach the roof, where the blood continues.
Follow it to the pigeon coop. There you will find an envelope with the name A. Maldonado written on it. The envelope is empty.
Pick up the trail again and you’ll find a gold-plated make-up case on the ground. Then follow the trail all the way to a drainpipe that leads to the next roof. Climb up that.
Follow the blood once more to a box which has another item dangling from a string, this time it is the ring taken from Antonia’s finger.
Hop to the next level and find a bucket with what appears to be Antonia’s blood inside, and a paintbrush. Guess this is what has been smearing the blood everywhere. This updates the blood trail clue.

Follow the blood once more to the corner of the roof, and you’ll find the other half of the library card. This confirms the victim's full name as Antonia Maldonado, and gives you her address. This finally wraps up your investigation of the crime scene.
Next, you’ll want to travel to Antonia’s residence.

blocks.title: Antonia’s Boarding House

topics.response: Phelps first asks if anybody would like to harm Antonia. Barbara replies with “That rat of a husband, Angel”. She doesn’t seem to like the man. She mentions the divorce papers as a motive, and looks you dead in the eye. Believe her, and she goes on to say that Angel was a cruel husband to Antonia, who was a good girl, if slightly religious.

Phelps asks when Antonia left and where she went the previous day. Barbara gives a time, but says she has no idea where she went. However, she can’t look you in the eyes as she says it, and she admits to knowing that Antonia went to the El Dorado Bar, noting that she had been drinking a lot lately. Rusty adds that the bar is close to the murder scene.

topics.instruction: Evidence of Break-In: Accuse - Broken Window or Iron Picket
topics.response: Phelps asks about the break in, and Barbara denies that there had been a break in. Of course, you know there was, so call her on it and use either the window or the picket as evidence. She then confesses to hearing a noise in the early hours of the morning, but didn’t want her boarding house to get a reputation, so was going to keep it quiet.

topics.instruction: Breakdown of Marriage: Accuse - Charm Bracelet Photograph
topics.response: Phelps asks about the state of the marriage between Angel and Antonia. She claims that Antonia moved in 2 months earlier. Phelps points out that she still wore her wedding ring, and Barbara adds that she wore a religious necklace, but nothing else. You know that she did wear other jewelry though, so bring up the photo you found, and Barbara tells you that she never wore the bracelet, as it was a gift from Angel. And that she kept it in her wooden jewelry box.

paragraphs: Travel to the boarding house. You’ll be let in by Barbara Lapenti. Phelps reports the murder of Antonia to the woman, and asks if he can search Antonia’s bedroom. Head upstairs and approach room 5.

Enter the room and you will find that it has been broken into and ransacked. Turn right and examine the Broken Window, and see the Iron Picket lying outside on the balcony. When you finish, Phelps automatically crawls through the window to examine the Picket more closely, and wonders where it came from.

Re-enter the room and find the face down Charm Bracelet Photograph on the dresser. You get a close up of the bracelet, which was curiously missing from her items you found at the crime scene. Examine the suitcase to find an envelope addressed to Mrs. Maldonado. Open it and scroll down to add the Attorney’s Letter to your clues, and find out that Antonia had filed for divorce from her husband. The letter gives you Angel Maldonado’s address.
Head back downstairs to interview the owner of the house.
Interview: Mrs. Lapenti.
Now that’s over with, fast travel to the Maldonado residence.

blocks.title: Maldonado Residence
paragraphs: Examine the mailboxes to discover that Angel is in apartment 304. Climb the stairs to the top floor to trigger a scene. Galloway busts into the house and places Angel under arrest. No sooner do you lower your guns though, when Angel’s brother gets a cheap shot in on Galloway. This starts a brawl with the brother, while Galloway takes on Angel himself. Use the usual techniques, and you’ll be fine. If you dispatch the brother quick enough, you can aid Rusty.

Once both brothers are cuffed, and a pick up car is ordered, Phelps breaks the news of Antonia’s death to Angel. He seems genuinely shocked and upset. When the guys have been hauled off, you get chance to look around.

Enter the kitchen first, where you’ll find the Bloodied Shirt on the laundry line. Next, examine the crate on the floor to get the address for Just Picked Fruit Market, which seems kind of random until you find a lot of booze inside the crate. There is also a matchbox from the El Dorado bar, which gives you the address if you don’t already have it from the previous interview. Rusty suggests you go talk to the neighbours.

Exit the apartment and start knocking on doors. Room 305’s occupant worked nights the previous night and knows nothing. Room 301 is good for a laugh. The key room is 302, where the woman tells you that she heard a fight from the Maldonado’s last night, and that Antonia left with Angel following her, and neither returned all night. This gives you the husband’s alibi clue.
After this, Galloway suggests you head to the El Dorado bar next. As you get in the car to do so, Donnelly requests you return to Central Station, so you best get down there first.

blocks.title: Central Station
paragraphs: Head inside and approach the front desk to get the location of Donnelly. Follow Rusty and you’ll find him with Ray Pinker and Finis Brown.
The Black Dahlia killer has left two notes for you to view. Look at them both, and go through some cut scenes about the premise of the note, and the 5 men wondering what the killer has planned.
Now, while we’re here, we can interview Angel. He’s in interview room 2.

blocks.title: Angel Maldonado

topics.instruction: Last contact with Victim: Accuse - Husband’s Alibi
topics.response: Phelps asks when Angel last saw his wife, and he replies that she came round briefly the night before. You know that’s not the full story, so bring up the alibi you got from the neighbour, and Angel tells you that his wife jumped in a Brown Ford Coupe, and it was too dark to identify the driver

topics.instruction: Jewelry taken from the body: Good Cop
topics.response: Phelps asks about the religious necklace, and whether Antonia was wearing it the night before. Angel confirms she was. Believe him, and you ask about the bracelet, which Angel says she never wore, confirming what you already knew.

topics.instruction: Divorce Proceedings: Accuse - Attorney’s Letter (Divorce Papers if you visited El Dorado bar before this interview)
topics.response: When Phelps asks about the fighting, Angel attempts to deny that there was going to be a divorce. However, you have seen evidence against this. Use the Attorney’s Letter you found, or the Divorce Papers provided in the El Dorado bar if you went there first. Angel gives some more details about the incident last night, and Phelps also gets a shoe size, size 8.

Phelps asks about the bloodied shirt you found in the apartment. Angel says he cut himself shaving. A likely story. but he changes the story to getting into a fight with his brother. He goes on to say Antonia’s visit to the El Dorado bar reminded him of the Just Picked Fruit Market, where his wife would be ogled by a ‘creep’.

paragraphs: Time to get out of here. You’ll want to go to the El Dorado bar next.

blocks.title: El Dorado bar
paragraphs: When you enter the El Dorado bar, you automatically speak to the bartender, Diego Aguilar. He worked the previous night, and says that Antonia was hammered, and left a letter behind. Examine it for the Divorce Papers clue, which updates your Attorney’s Letter. Finish examining the papers and the interview sequence will start.

blocks.title: Diego Aguilar

topics.response: Diego states that Antonia left the bar with the intention of serving the divorce papers to her husband. His look suggests this is all he knows. Believe him, and Phelps asks if the other patrons were giving her much attention, which he says they were, but she scared them off.

Phelps asks about the jewelry that Antonia was wearing, and Diego mentions the religious necklace, and says she was talking to the temporary bar staff most of the night. Phelps then asks when she left, but Diego says he doesn’t know. He looks a little shifty though, and he admits that she wanted to call a cab, but the phone is out of order, so he sent her over to the Just Picked Fruit Market across the road.

paragraphs: After the interview, head out the back door for a scene involving a man making deliveries from the Fruit Market. When Phelps brings up the box of booze you found earlier, he denies all knowledge, and drives off in his truck.
Next, you’ll want to be head to the Fruit Market.

blocks.title: Just Picked Fruit Market
paragraphs: Enter the market to talk to the proprietor, who is the same guy you just saw. His name is Clem Feeney, and he says that Antonia did come by the store last night.

blocks.title: Clem Feeney

topics.response: Phelps asks if she was wearing her necklace last night. Feeney claims not to know, but looks a bit shifty, so select Bad Cop him. Phelps brings up why the store is open at midnight, and Feeney admits to selling booze on the side.

Feeney says the lady arrived around midnight, used his phone, called a cab and left. He looks nervous though and he says that he has spoken to her before, but her husband always got jealous, and he’d not seen her in a while.

Feeney says that Antonia was unable to get a cab, and got into a car that pulled up. Believe him, and he goes on to say it was a brown Ford Coupe that was mentioned in Angel’s interview. Feeney adds that Antonia seemed to know the driver.

paragraphs: Phelps then asks if they can look around. Clem doesn’t like the idea, but Galloway says he has no choice.
This triggers a scene and Feeney takes off running, and climbs into his delivery truck.

Clem veers through back alleys and over pavements. Be careful as you follow not to run over any civilians, because that will count against you in your rating. Drive quickly but carefully until Clem reaches the streets, then pull up alongside him to have Galloway shoot out his tires to catch him and close the case.

vehicleOpportunities.note: Parked in the raised parking lot behind the Maldonado residence in “The Silk Stocking Murder”, or in the parking lot across the street from Central Station in “The Red Lipstick Murder”

vehicleOpportunities.name: Pontiac Torpedo Six
vehicleOpportunities.note: Parking lot behind Maldonado residence in “The Silk Stocking Murder”, or Boxing stadium car park in “The Set Up”

vehicleOpportunities.name: Oldsmobile Hydramatic 88
vehicleOpportunities.note: Parking lot by the Just Picked Fruit Market in “The Silk Stocking Murder”, or the Hall of Records Parking Lot in “The Quarter Moon Murders”

vehicleOpportunities.note: Parking lot behind the Maldonado residence in “The Silk Stocking Murder”, or near the crime scene in “The White Shoe Slaying”

cases.title: The White Shoe Slaying
objectives: Investigate the crime scene and interview Catherine Barton
Investigate Taraldsen Residence and interview Lars Taraldsen
Investigate Baron’s Bar and interview Benny Cluff
Interview James Jessop at Central Station
Investigate Hobo Camp and Arrest Stuart Ackerman
Interview Stuart Ackerman at Central Station

blocks.title: Briefing
paragraphs: At the start of the case, you see an attractive and visibly drunk lady step off a bus in the rain. Oblivious to the rain, she tries to make her way home, and nearly gets hit by a car. Behind a fence, somebody is watching with great interest.
The next day, the storm is still going, and Donnelly announces there is another case for you, a woman dumped on Signal Hill.

blocks.title: Signal Hill Crime Scene
paragraphs: Head to the crime scene and speak to Carruthers and Pinker. You see a familiar scene, murdered woman, strangled and with blunt force trauma to her head. He places the time of Death at around 2AM. Pinker adds that a lot of the evidence has been washed away in the storm. Great.

Phelps notes that she is clothed, and has no writing on her body this time. The green dress is very distinctive, and she is missing a white shoe. Carruthers also points out that there is no other personal effects lying about, and there are tire tracks leading away from the scene.

Examine the body. Move her head until you get a close up of the laundry label in the back of her dress. Phelps notes the number and place. Look at the hands to see there is no missing jewelry this time.

At an evidence marker you find Boot Prints running from the body to a set of tire tracks at another marker. That’s it for this scene. Head to the nearest game well to call in the Superior Laundry lead, but as you step out of the crime scene, you get a delivery of a woman named Catherine Barton. There is a short interview.

blocks.title: Catherine Barton

topics.response: Catherine didn’t spot anybody around late last night, but she does say ‘that awful Hobo’ was sneaking around during the day. This adds hobo to you POI. She seems honest, and she came forward with the information, so there’s no reason not to believe her. She goes on to describe the hobo as being a very scary, angry man, tall, gaunt and horribly disfigured. She mentions he seems to be some sort of hobo leader, and suspects you could find him in one of the hobo camps in the area. Hobo gets updated to disfigured man in your POI.

paragraphs: Now, use that game well you were heading towards. Call in the superior laundry lead, and also inquire about hobo camps near the murder scene. You get a location for both. We’re going to be heading to superior laundry first, so fast travel there and listen to Galloway talk about how the case cannot be related to the other cases, as there is no writing and she wasn’t left on display.

blocks.title: Superior Laundry Services
paragraphs: Approach the service deck to trigger a scene where Phelps asks about the laundry label you found. Check out the ledger that the man hands to you, and find F1363, a green silk dress, which belongs to Mrs. T Taraldsen. You also get her address. Fast travel there next.

blocks.title: Taraldsen Residence
paragraphs: When you knock on the Taraldsen’s door, it is answered by a man who introduces himself as Lars Taraldsen. He says his wife hasn’t returned from a party at the house of Bobby Ross the previous night. He describes the green dress and white shoes she was wearing, and then Phelps breaks the news that his wife is dead. Galloway tells the man to see to his two children while they search the house.
Look around the bookshelf to find a chess board with a Baron’s Bar matchbook on. This gives you the address and adds the location to your map.
Head to the bedroom and find the dresser, where you’ll find another matchbook and a photo of the Taraldsens, curiously turned down.

Now search the laundry room. Find the victim’s handbag on the side. Open it and find the lipstick, which Phelps remarks that at least she didn’t have to go through that too. Examine her driver's licence to find that her full name was Theresa Taraldsen.

Turn around and examine the Wet Jacket hanging on the door. It seems that Lars was out in the rain last night. Then examine the muddy boots, which are a familiar size 8. Phelps wonders if it can be matched to the crime scene.
Search the yard next and find a boat tied up with some Bow Rope. Phelps notes that it could well be a match to the ligature marks on the victim’s body.
Call KGPL using the phone on the side to ask for a uniformed officer to be sent to Bobby Ross to confirm Lars’ whereabouts the previous night. Then head back to the living room to interview Lars.

blocks.title: Lars Taraldsen

topics.response: Phelps asks Lars if he knows anybody who may have wanted to harm his wife. He replies that everybody loves Theresa, and it couldn’t be someone who knew her. But he swallows heavily and avoids eye contact. Use the Bow Rope (I’m not sure why this is right either, but it is) as evidence and Phelps goes in for the kill, outlining that Lars killed his wife after being embarrassed at the party by her. Phelps notes that the rope matches the ligature marks on her neck, but Lars just seems upset that he let his wife go.

topics.instruction: Alibi for Lars Taraldsen: Bad Cop
topics.response: Phelps asks about the party. Lars answers that people were having fun but Theresa got bored and left. This may be the truth, but it's probably not the whole story, and he says that Theresa likes to go dancing, but Lars wanted to stay at the Ross party. He says she normally goes to Baron’s Bar and calls him to get her when she is suitably drunk.

topics.instruction: Victim’s State of Mind: Bad Cop
topics.response: Phelps asks if Theresa seemed happy with her life. Lars replies that she was, but can’t keep the look out of his eye that everything wasn’t quite so rosy, and he reveals that he was angry and tired at her impulsive nature, and that’s why he let her leave the party alone. He says she left the party around 8.30PM

topics.instruction: Last Contact with Victim: Accuse - Wet Jacket/Muddy Boots
topics.response: Apparently, when Theresa left, Lars wrapped up the card game and then left, coming straight home to bed. But you know this can’t be quite true, with the state of the jacket and boots in the laundry. So call him and use either one, and he says that he walked a lady home first, before going home. He looks distraught.

paragraphs: Phelps lets the man off, telling him to come to identify his wife’s body, and also tells Galloway that his story seems to ring true a little.
Time to check out Baron’s Bar.

blocks.title: Baron’s Bar
paragraphs: Travel to the Baron’s Bar and approach the Bartender. He says his name is Benny Cluff, and says that he heard about Theresa’s death on the radio. He says he tried to ring the husband the previous night, but the babysitter said he wasn’t home.

blocks.title: Benny Cluff

topics.instruction: Last Contact with Victim: Good Cop
topics.response: Benny says that Theresa left the bar around 10.30PM last night. Believe him, and he goes on to say she left in a cab, and that he got the number. He hands over a piece of paper with ‘Yellow Cab 3591’ written on it. This adds a new question to your interview.

Phelps asks about the hobo and gives a description. Cluff says that he gets a few vagrants in his bar, but nobody fitting that description. He looks a little uneasy though and he reveals that Theresa had the attention of numerous creeps the previous night. One was a sailor in uniform, the other was Richard Bates, who is in the bar right now in the red polo shirt.

Phelps asks if Cluff knows where Theresa was going in the cab the previous night. He says he doesn’t, which is fine. Believe him, and he says that she was trying to talk some of the guys into going dancing with her, which she always wanted to do after a drink.

paragraphs: After the interview, head over to Bates, who takes off when you introduce yourselves. He runs straight across the street, causing a car to screech to a halt. As the driver of the car gets out to yell at Bates, commandeer his vehicle, as Bates jumps into his pickup truck. Stay on Bates’ trail as he meanders through alleyways and through a gas station. He then speeds down a hill. Do your best to disable his car, but if you don’t, he ends up trying to escape on foot, and you can get him using a tackle, a warning shot, or wait until he surrenders after being cornered.

blocks.title: Richard Bates

topics.response: Bates was drinking with Theresa the previous night, but he claims to have lost out to a sailor she preferred. His face looks nervous though, Phelps threatens to let Galloway get rough on the guy. Bates reveals that Theresa was drunk, angry with her husband, and wanted to go dancing, which we already knew.

Bates says that the sailor nailed him with a cheap shot after they left the bar. He says he can’t remember much after that. Phelps gets him to reveal that he is on parole for sexual assault, but sticks to the story that the sailor decked him and took off in a taxi.

paragraphs: After the interview, Bates is hauled away by uniformed officers, and you can return to your car. You can get more information on Bates’ story by using the game well, but hold off on that for the moment, and get into your car. Phelps asks Galloway to call in the cab number and request any sightings be sent to your car.

blocks.title: Yellow Cab Trace
paragraphs: Next you’re going to be doing a little taxi hunting. As you drive, you get a call saying that the cab has been spotted at a gas station of 7th near Garland. It appears as a yellow dot on your map. Head there as fast as you can, when you arrive, the car has moved, and you get an update saying that it is a few blocks away. Drive there as quick as you can, and if you get there in time, you yellow dot will change to a red car indicator. If you’re not fast enough, it continues to move until you finally catch up to it. Remember, speed may be of the essence, but don’t cause any damage or you risk your 5 star rating.

Pull up to the cab when you find it, and question the cabbie. He says that the sailor mentioned before was all over Theresa, but she pushed him off and said she just wanted to dance. She was dropped off at Crystal Ballroom at 12.30AM
Now it's time to use the nearest game well. You discover that a sailor named James Jessop has checked himself into Central Station. Head there now.

blocks.title: Central Station
paragraphs: Approach the desk and find out where Jessop is being held. Head for interview room 2.

blocks.title: James Jessop

topics.response: Just a quick note, you’re doubting everything this man says in this interview, if you wanted to rush through it. Jessop says he arrived at the Baron’s Bar at 7PM, where he met Theresa. He says they had a couple of drinks, but he looks nervous, and you know there was more to it and he will say that he tried to make it with the girl, and they caught a cab to the Crystal Ballroom, which collates to the cabbie’s statement.

When asked about his fight with Richard Bates, he says that Bates is a creep and you should be looking into him for the murder. But he looks off to the side afterwards, and will admit to punching Bates, but then says that she was better off with Jessop anyway.

topics.instruction: Cab Ride with Victim: Bad Cop
topics.response: You only get this topic if you followed the cab first. Phelps says that the cabbie thought Jessop got a little too friendly with Theresa. Jessop vaguely replies “That’s not how I’d put it”. Go Bad Cop on him and he makes no apologies for his advances on the woman, but says she was having none of it anyway. At the Crystal Ballroom, she apparently drank more and her attention went to a bartender over him anyway.

topics.instruction: Movements Prior to Murder: Bad Cop
topics.response: Jessop says that when they left the Crystal Ballroom, he took a bus back to base, while Theresa caught a cab. But he looks evasive, and he reveals that she did indeed get on the bus with him, fell asleep on his shoulder, and got off at her stop. He continued on the ride to base. He tells you the bus’ details as an All American 249.

paragraphs: Phelps orders that Jessop continue to be detained until his story can be confirmed. An officer informs Phelps that the hobo has been spotted on Grand, near the hobo camp, and is wanted for the assault of two other females previously. Sounds like a hot suspect, but you’ll want to clear Jessop’s story first, so head to the Bus Depot.

blocks.title: Interstate Bus Depot
paragraphs: Enter the building and ask who was driving the 249 the previous night. The clerk gives his name as Frank Zeferelli, and gives you a map of the route he is currently driving on. Check your map, and the route is highlighted in red. Exit your map, and your minimap will also have it highlighted.

Your goal is to simply drive around the route until you find the All American 74. Keep following the red line. You’ll feel like you’ll never find the thing, but eventually, Galloway shouts that the bus is there, and says you should put your siren on to pull him over. Do so, and the bus will stop for you. Get out and approach the bus for details of the previous night from the driver. He remembers the two, and says that he took the sailor all the way downtown, and let the girl off near the hobo camp, but felt uneasy doing so as she didn’t seem to know where she was. This gives you the Victim Last Seen clue.
Next, travel to the Hobo Camp.

blocks.title: Hobo Camp
paragraphs: Travel to the camp and get out. You discover that Galloway keeps a very handy shotgun on him. Galloway guns down a few bums, then the rest scarper, except the leader, who calls the detectives Fascists. Phelps ends up in a fistfight with him. Knock him out, and afterwards, you learn your attacker’s name, Stuart Ackerman.
A uniformed officer arrives and hauls Ackerman downtown for questioning. You get the chance to freely examine the camp. You only need to search the corrugated shack in front of you though.

Inside the shack, be sure to pick up the sixth newspaper and watch the cinematic behind the headlines. Next, find the bloodstained rope piece on the nightstand next to the bed. Examine it closely, and it looks like triple braid, the usual method you’ve seen recently.
On the table across the room you find a war photograph and a purse with the initials T.T on it. Examine it to find a stubbed Crystal Ballroom ticket inside. Doesn’t look good.
Head back to the Central Police Station.

blocks.title: Stuart Ackerman

topics.instruction: Motive For Murder: Accuse - Bloodstained Rope Piece
topics.response: Phelps asks straight up why Ackerman chose to kill Theresa. Ackerman gives a very vague answer, and looks away. You have evidence to prove he did though, so bring up the rope you found in his shack, and he states that he owns no property, so it cannot belong to him. I don’t think that would stick in court.

topics.instruction: Contact with the Victim: Bad Cop
topics.response: Phelps asks why Ackerman took Theresa up the hill after she got off the bus. Ackerman replies “Which hill? I have many places”, which is an odd answer and Phelps says that the man is insane and won’t face the death penalty. Ackerman then confesses to killing many women. Strange interview technique.

topics.instruction: Alibi For Stuart Ackerman: Accuse - Purse
topics.response: Phelps asks for the whereabouts of Ackerman at 2.00AM that morning. He replies that he was in the camp. So the purse magically appeared there right? Bring it up and Ackerman says more strange confessions, and Phelps has enough and charges Ackerman with murder. Case closed.

paragraphs: Enter the room and Phelps guesses that the man was in the Marine Corps when he recognises the burns that the man has.

vehicleOpportunities.note: The vehicle stops in front of you when you chase Richard Bates in “The White Shoe Slaying”

vehicleOpportunities.name: Plymouth Sedan
vehicleOpportunities.note: Parking lot behind the Maldonado residence in “The Silk Stocking Murder”, or near the crime scene in “The White Shoe Slaying”

vehicleOpportunities.name: Chevrolet Pickup
vehicleOpportunities.note: Beside Schroeder’s apartment in “Upon Reflection”, or in the alley as you exit the Hobo Camp in “The White Shoe Slaying”

cases.title: The Studio Secretary Murder
objectives: Investigate Railyard Crime Scene and Interview Jamison
Investigate Mensch’s Bar and Interview McCaffrey
Investigate Levine’s Liquor Store and Interview Robbins
Return to Mensch’s Bar and Interview McCaffrey again
Meet Captain at Central Police Station
Go to Rawlings Bowling Alley and Apprehend Tiernan
Investigate McCaffrey’s Apartment and Apprehend McCaffrey
Interrogate Tiernan and McCaffrey at Central Police Station

blocks.title: Briefing
paragraphs: The opening scene shows a drunk and unkempt woman staggering through a train yard at night. She is being stalked by a man carrying a tire iron. When the train passes, he makes his move.

Cut to the station, and Donnelly reports some slightly disturbing news. The rings taken from Deirdre Moller in the Golden Butterfly Case have been pawned. Donnelly wants the pawnbroker to be quietly pressed for information, as the case goes up before the grand jury soon, and they want a conviction.
There’s also a new crime scene to investigate, at the rail freight depot, where another woman has been murdered.
Fast Travel to Globe Loan and Jewelry.

blocks.title: Globe Loan and Jewelry
paragraphs: Enter the pawn shop and speak to the owner. The man is David Bremner, and he has the wedding and engagement rings mentioned. Galloway does a little hard bargaining, and you gain possession of the rings. You examine each one in turn, the first one, examine it to be told about the hallmark stamp, indicating quality. The second ring has the maker’s mark on it, telling you that the ring was made in Hartfield’s Jewelry on Broadway.
The pawnbroker states that the man gave his name as Percy B Shelley, and left an address. He says the man was one of those men you just forget.

Exit the shop and fast travel to the Railyard Crime Scene. Listen to the conversation carefully, as Phelps makes links between the Black Dahlia killer and the Deirdre Moller murder. The key being the name and address given to the pawnbroker, which are fakes. Shelley was also the name of the author of the poems received earlier in the game.

blocks.title: Railyard Crime Scene
paragraphs: When you arrive at the crime scene, a uniformed officer tells you to follow him to the body. Follow the car, and Galloway tells Phelps to keep the new information under wraps for the moment, until the chain of command sees fit to release it.

Get out of your car and trigger a meeting with Officer Hart. He has two guys for you to interview, a guy named Jamison, and a rail worker, Nelson Gaines. He goes to keep an eye on Jamison while you search the area.

Approach the body and the coroner to talk to him. He points out the lipstick smudges on her face, but no writing, blunt force trauma to the head and ligature marks. He estimates the time of death as being sometime after midnight.

Examine the body. Phelps first notices the smell, which Carruther’s seems to point to a period of Vagrancy, or homelessness. Examine the right hand to find there is a missing ring, once again removed from her body.

Right, rest of the crime scene now. There are items laid out on a mat nearby. Examine the handbag and open it. Take out the pink slip of paper, which gives you the victim’s name, Evelyn Summers, and also suggests that she once had a movie lot job in the legal department. Unfortunately, Keystone Company’s closed six years ago.

Next, take out the half torn up letter, which shows that Evelyn had a drink problem. Somebody was trying to get her to come home. This is the last part that’s useful with the handbag. Next, pick up the sheet of paper, which is a list of personal items from Levine’s Liquor Store, which adds the store to your locations to call for an address later.
Finally, pick up the matchbox to see an address for Mensch’s Bar, which gives you another location to look into. After a quick chat to Pinker, you can start you interviews.

Firstly, approach the African American man in overalls to trigger a conversation. He found the woman, with your other interviewee on top of her, at 7.30 this morning, hours after the estimated time of death.
Now, head over to Jamison. When Phelps asks what he was doing with the body, Jamison admits that he was kissing her. Galloway doesn’t seem particularly happy with this revelation.
Phelps asks the man to turn out his pockets, and he produces some lipstick, which has been used. He claims he found it on the ground near the purse. This starts your interview sequence.

blocks.title: John Ferdinand Jamison

topics.instruction: Discovery of Victim’s Body: Bad Cop
topics.response: Jamison says that he found the body as he was getting off shift. This may seem honest enough, but his shifty expression tells you there is more to tell and he says when he came past this part of the railyard at midnight she wasn’t there, and then this morning she was, and he knew she was dead.

When Phelps asks why Jamison went through the victim’s purse, he admits it, justifying it with “it wasn’t as if she needed it”. He’s got a point, but it's still not right. He goes on to say there was no money in the purse, and he found the lipstick and matchbook on the mat. Phelps puts Jamison under arrest, to which he says he did nothing illegal, eliciting another response from Rusty.

paragraphs: Galloway suggests that you check out Mensch’s Bar next, but before you do, call in the Liquor Store lead on the game well behind your car. Then fast travel to Mensch’s.

blocks.title: Mensch’s Bar
paragraphs: You automatically enter the bar and trigger a scene, where Phelps chats to the owner, Walter Mensch, about Evelyn Summers. Mensch paints a picture of an unpleasant, penniless woman who bummed drinks off patrons. He suggests to ask around about her.
The guy by the front window doesn’t have that much to say, other than confirming that she always used to mooch drinks off people.
Approach the man who is reading in one of the booths. He is Grosvenor McCaffrey, a writer. He agrees to talk about Summers, but says he didn’t really know her, but was aware of her.

blocks.title: Grosvenor McCaffrey

topics.instruction: Last Contact With Victim: Bad Cop
topics.response: Phelps asks if he saw Evelyn the previous night. He replies that he was at home writing, but doesn’t sound convincing. When Phelps says that he is going to start getting interested in him for the case, McCaffrey opens up a little more, and points the finger at a man named Tiernan, saying him and Evelyn used to spend time together at the library, and that he works for the bowling alley. This adds both Tiernan and the Bowling alley to your notebook.

Phelps asks if McCaffrey has a criminal record. He claims to have had a few minor skirmishes, nothing serious, but seems evasive and he admits that he was involved in strikes and workers’ rights issues. Galloway points out that this means he is a Communist.

paragraphs: Next, fast travel to Levine’s Liquor Store.

blocks.title: Levine’s Liquor Store
paragraphs: Enter the store and talk to a man named Robbins, the owner. He knew Evelyn Summers, and was a good friend of her ex-husband apparently. He kept some of her things in his store. Follow Robbins through the store to see some of Evelyn’s items.

Enter the curtained off area, and turn left to pick up a statuette labelled “Keystone Films 1938”. Robbins tells you that Evelyn worked for the studio’s legal copyrights for music. There is also a Keystone nameplate, and a Rawling’s Bowling pin.

Now check the opposite corner of the area. Pick up the framed photograph to see that Evelyn wasn’t always a loner. Then examine the book, Aristotle’s Metaphysics, which is pretty heavy reading for an alcoholic. Robbins said the only bad thing about Evelyn was her need to drink. Open the book, and you’ll find a familiar name written there, Grosvenor McCaffrey. Seems the man had more than an awareness of Evelyn Summers.
Now it's time to interview Robbins to get a wider picture.

blocks.title: Walter Robbins

topics.response: Phelps wants to account for the movements of Evelyn the day before. Robbins says that he saw her earlier in the day, and she bought a bottle of Rye. He’s an honest man, so believe him, and he adds that Evelyn didn’t tell him where she got the money, but did say that the liquor purchase was a make-up present for a boy who she had been fighting with.

Robbins admits that he will probably be one of the few people who is sad that Evelyn is gone. Again, he’s being very real with you, so believe him. He says that she was slipping deeper into her alcoholism. Robbins fears he may not have helped her by providing a place to stay.

Robbins isn’t quite as honest about McCaffrey, merely saying he didn’t know the man personally. But he’s evasive and he says that McCaffrey was idolised by Evelyn because of his revolutionary stance on society. He suggests that McCaffrey didn’t have the same view about Evelyn.

paragraphs: After the interview, get back into your car (make sure you are driving, not your partner) to get a call from KGPL for you to return to Central Station. However, you have a lead you need to follow first so return to Mensch’s Bar. If you do not do this now, you will lose the chance to do it, missing a clue and an interview question.

blocks.title: Mensch’s Bar
paragraphs: Enter the bar.

blocks.title: Grosvenor McCaffrey

topics.response: Phelps mentions that McCaffrey barely knew Evelyn. He reaffirms this, but looks a little shifty. Bring up the book you found, and he reports that Evelyn was last seen with Tiernan, entering a hotel with a bottle of booze.

paragraphs: Head out of the bar with the new clue, and fast travel to Central Police Station.

blocks.title: Central Police Station
paragraphs: Time to meet with the captain. Head downstairs to technical services and find Carruthers, Pinker and Donnelly. Your arrival triggers a scene. The three of them are finally concerned about the similarities between the Henry, Moller, Taraldson and now Summers murders. Donnelly and Galloway see it as just being copycats, people who have read about the previous murder and think they can get away with it. Carruthers points out that the killer has been using the same lipstick, the B.D killer, and other details suggesting there is more to it than that. The captains asks the detectives to keep the concerns quiet for the moment, and break the Summers case.
Use the phone on your way out to trace the address for Grosvenor McCaffrey, before fast travelling to the Bowling Alley.

blocks.title: Rawling’s Bowling Alley
paragraphs: Upon arrival, the detectives automatically enter and speak to the woman at the desk. She tells you that Tiernan does indeed work there, and directs you around the back. Walk around the left hand side of all the lanes, and you’ll spot Tiernan running through a staff door. Follow him to trigger a chase. Tiernan reaches his car and speeds off, but you manage to commandeer a car for yourselves and follow him

Tiernan takes a high speed route that criss-crosses through Pershing Square and eventually leads you into the Red Line Tunnel. Follow him and try to gain enough ground to let Rusty shoot his tires out. When you finally bring him to a halt, a wagon carts him off to the station so that you can question him later. Now it's time to head to McCaffrey’s apartment.

blocks.title: McCaffrey’s Apartment

clues.name: Torn Letter (Updates upper half of torn letter)

paragraphs: Fast travel to the apartment and then examine the mailboxes to find out where you are going. You want apartment 6, so head upstairs and find the right one. Approach the door to knock, and then kick it in.

Head to the living room on the left to find the bottom half of the letter you found earlier, which updates to a full letter in your clues, which tells you that the letter was from Evelyn’s mother, Augusta. Close to this on the right is a blood splattered tire iron that you should be used to finding by now. There is also a bloody shirt, but that isn’t a clue. If you examine the tire iron, you find that it has “Rawling’s Bowling” written on it.

Right then, a woman enters calling for McCaffrey. She says she is a neighbour, and tells the detectives that he has a pigeon coop on the roof, and you should check there. Head up to the third floor and then find the roof access sign to find the stairs to take you to the coop.

Your arrival at the roof triggers another chase. McCaffrey spots the detectives, and takes off. He crosses a walkway and then heads down the fire escape. Remember, to catch up quicker, slide down the ladders so you don’t lose him. McCaffrey sprints up a wooden staircase, and then heads through yards and alleys to try to lose you. As you get close, tap the tackle button to close him down and take him out. He gets hauled off by another wagon, and now it's time to cross examine the two suspects. Head back to the station.

blocks.title: Central Police Station
paragraphs: Donnelly is waiting for you when you arrive. He says he wants a confession from one of the guys. This is one of the trickiest sequences in the game, and you’ll be interviewing each man twice before charging. Let's get this case finished then. First, head to Interview Room 1 to interview Tiernan

blocks.title: James Tiernan

topics.instruction: Relationship With Victim: Accuse - Victim Last Seen
topics.response: When asked, he says that he barely knew Evelyn Summers. You know that this is a bit of a stretch, so call him out on the lie and use Victim Last Seen against him. Tiernan says that he did indeed go for a drink with her at his hotel, but he passed out and when he woke up, she was gone.

Phelps asks about the copy of the book that you found with McCaffrey’s name. He says she was interested in it, but McCaffrey laughed at her for it. Apparently, she stole it to have a piece of McCaffrey, but there’s something he’s not telling you, and Tiernan suggests that McCaffrey’s criminal record is something more than you have been told.

topics.instruction: Alibi for James Tiernan: Accuse - Liquor Purchase
topics.response: Phelps tries to tie the two together for the night by saying Evelyn had nowhere else to stay after drinking with Tiernan. He continues to deny knowledge of what happened that night. Bring up the liquor purchase that was made for someone Evelyn was fighting with. He then admits that there was more than friendship between the two, but her worshipping of McCaffrey upset him, and he kicked her out.

topics.instruction: Access to Murder Weapon: Bad Cop
topics.response: Tiernan doesn’t own a car, but admits to using lug wrenches at the bowling alley. The Tire Iron you found at McCaffrey’s was from the alley, however, there’s no evidence to suggest it was Tiernan, and Phelps makes the accusation that he planted the weapon. Tiernan gives a full accusation to what happened, that Evelyn stole the book from McCaffrey, and McCaffrey threatened her life when he found out. This gives you Tiernans Accusation as a clue.

paragraphs: Leave the interview and head over to interview room 2 to try your luck with McCaffrey.

blocks.title: Grosvenor McCaffrey

topics.instruction: Alibi for McCaffrey: Accuse - Torn Letter
topics.response: Phelps asks McCaffrey where he was at the time of Evelyn’s death. He says that he was at home writing. However, you have evidence that ties him to the scene, so bring up the torn letter, and he changes his story, claiming no knowledge, and that the letter was planted.

topics.instruction: Access to Tire Iron: Accuse - Tiernans Accusation
topics.response: Phelps then confronts McCaffrey about the weapon found at his apartment. The man says he wouldn’t stupid enough to keep a murder weapon in his own apartment. He claims that Evelyn was too insignificant to bother with, but Tiernans statement claims otherwise, so bring it up and McCaffrey turns it right back at Tiernan. He says that Tiernan killed Summers, then came to McCaffrey for help. McCaffrey agreed to dispose of the weapon and bloodied shirt. Phelps seems unconvinced, but that’s McCaffrey’s Accusation for you.

paragraphs: Leave the interview room again and head back to interview 1 to bring up the new claims against Tiernan.

blocks.title: James Tiernan

topics.instruction: Events Prior to Murder: Accuse - McCaffrey’s Accusation
topics.response: Phelps asks again what happened in Tiernans hotel room. Tiernan says he simply woke up hungover and alone. Bring up what McCaffrey has just said to you, and Tiernan breaks down. He says he was angry, possibly angry enough to kill her, but he has no memory of actually doing so. He seems distraught.

paragraphs: LEAVE THE INTERVIEW!
You cannot get 5 stars by charging Tiernan, so despite the fact that he’s just practically confessed to the murder, you must leave the interview.

blocks.title: R&I Phone Call
paragraphs: Before going back to McCaffrey, time to pick up one last clue. Use the phone to get messages from R&I. McCaffrey’s criminal record comes back in, and you learn he was convicted of petty theft, but also dishonourably discharged from the Army for beating a woman near to death. Head back to Interview Room 2 to discuss this with McCaffrey.

blocks.title: Grosvenor McCaffrey

topics.instruction: Military service: Accuse - McCaffrey’s Criminal Record
topics.response: McCaffrey says that the war changed him, that he saw terrible things and wanted to become a writer and make some changes. Phelps brings up the petty theft record, and McCaffrey says that he has never been convicted of anything violent. You know differently though, so bring up the record, and McCaffrey loses it, saying that the “peasant whore” tried to steal from his wallet. This is very similar to Evelyn stealing from him. When Phelps points this out, McCaffrey’s response is damning.

paragraphs: You now have evidence that can finish the case against both suspects. However, to get the 5 star rating, as I pointed out before, you must charge McCaffrey with the murder of Evelyn Summers. So charge him, and the case finishes with Donnelly praising your decision to charge the Communist over the Cry Baby.

vehicleOpportunities.name: Cisitalia Coupe
vehicleOpportunities.note: Wilshire Division 7, hidden behind the Angel City Security garage door of an Alaco station on the corner of Vermont Ave and Melrose Ave. You actually may have this, as you can use it to chase James Tiernan out the back of Rawling’s Bowling Alley in “The Studio Secretary Murder”

cases.title: The Quarter Moon Murders
objectives: Examine Items from the Black Dahlia Killer
Search Pershing Square Fountain to Find Evidence and a New Poem
Decipher Location Indicated in New Poem
Investigate New Location to Find Evidence and a New Poem
Repeat Process at Five More Locations

blocks.title: Briefing
paragraphs: This case isn’t really a case in such that you are investigating a murder, but following up on the Black Dahlia Killer mentioned through the homicide cases. You start the case in technical services, where Donnelly, Carruthers and Pinker have called Phelps and Galloway to look at the latest offering sent by the BD killer.

Pick up the Black Dahlia Letter constructed from cut-outs of newspapers. The message says the same words that were carved into the body of Theresa Taraldsen, and only the killer would know that information. It also challenges you to find him where he is hidden.

Pick up the red book by Shelley (remember, the last note was an excerpt from Shelley too) and find a passage from Prometheus Unbound has been bookmarked and underlined in red. Finally, pick up the paper for the Shelley Excerpt.

In this case, you will not have to memorise or note the excerpts down, they are noted in the clues book for you. If you need to read the excerpt again, simply select the relevant clue in your casebook.

The men all try to figure out some meaning behind all of this. The Excerpt seems to point to a specific LA landmark. In this case, Phelps points it out in the cutscene “I hid myself within a fountain in the public square”. This gives you your objective, to investigate Pershing Square. Pinker warns you that you are heading onto the maniac’s turf now.

blocks.title: Pershing Square Fountain
paragraphs: Travel to Pershing Square. Approach the fountain and walk around it in the lower pool until you hear your evidence chime. Climb up to the statue and find the two items at the statue’s base. Examine the social security card, which belonged to Elizabeth Short (The first victim, before you joined homicide), and also a second excerpt from Shelley (This updates “Shelley Excerpt” to “First Excerpt”)

This time, you have to decipher the clue yourself. The key words refer to an overgrown mountain cave with a frozen fountain hanging down from its curved roof. Open up your map and move your location to the Hall of Records, which is a couple of blocks northeast of your current location. The popup text mentions a domed skylight and a chandelier, which matches the description in the poem somewhat. Set it as your destination, and head there next.

blocks.title: Hall of Records
paragraphs: Head inside and talk to the desk guard. Phelps asks how to access the chandelier hanging from the skylight. He points you in the direction of a maintenance room on the top floor.

Climb up both flights of stairs and turn right at the top. Head into the second corridor on the left and enter the door marked ‘maintenance’. Approach the ladder on the far side of the room and climb to the top. Open the door to a small platform overlooking the atrium.

There is a length of cable running from the platform to the chandelier. Proceed carefully across the wire using the controls shown on the screen. Phelps grabs the wire if you fall off, but he only does this twice, on the third time, you will fail and have to start over.
Reach the chandelier and you’ll find Deidre Moller’s watch, and a third excerpt of Shelley’s poetry.
Once you have examined both items, the stabilizing cables snap, and you’ll have to swing the chandelier to safety. When you get close enough to the left, Phelps will automatically jump off to safety
The clue this time is pointing you to a “high temple”, which can be found at the public library. Head there next.

blocks.title: LA Public Library
paragraphs: When you arrive, you’ll see there is work being done to the library, and there is lots of scaffolding around the building. Phelps begins at the foot of a staircase. The climb is fairly linear, so you shouldn’t have trouble.

First, climb the stairs, then the drainpipe at the top on the right. Then use the low section of scaffold to get to the next roof. Turn right, and go to the next section of scaffolding. Pull yourself up and use the ladder to climb to the next platform. Turn right and cross the narrow plank. As before, you can fall twice.

Climb the next drainpipe and ladder, then make a running leap across the gaps, hopping from one scaffold to the next. Climb another ladder up two levels, and cross another narrow plank. At the far end of it, you’ll have to go down another ladder.

Slide down two levels of scaffold and go around the corner to hop down two more levels of scaffold to reach a ladder with several broken rungs. Climb up to reach some stairs and a final ladder, which takes you to the base of the tiled roof pyramid.
Follow the walkway around to the far corner and find Antonia’s Medallion and the Fourth Excerpt on the ground.
Reading the excerpt tells of “uncouth skeletons” that are “jammed in the hard, black deep”. Use your map to find the Westlake Tar Pits and set it as your destination.

blocks.title: Westlake Tar Pits
paragraphs: Phelps is in waders! So I guess we’d better wade. There are walkways just below the surface, which you can just make out when the camera changes to an overhead view. Be quick, as the planks are old and do not support your weight for too long. If you sink, you have to start over.
When you finally reach the island in the middle, you’ll find Theresa Taraldsen’s Shoe, and a fifth excerpt, which mentions a sphere set among wood rushes.

Galloway fetches you in a rowing boat (Thanks Rusty, I got my waders on for nothing), and you get to find where you’re going next. You’ll want to find the LA County Art Museum, which mentions its famous Armillary Sphere. Sounds good.

blocks.title: LA County Art Museum
paragraphs: Follow the signs that say “Way to Maze”, and then start working your way through to the centre of the maze. Head in, and follow the route to the first junction. Go right, and follow the path round, back upon yourself almost, to another junction where you can go left, right or straight on. Go right through the gap, and then immediately left, and follow the route past the next turn off, and round a couple of corners to the middle of the maze.
You’ll find Celine Henry’s Garnet Ring and the Sixth Excerpt in the middle of the maze. This one talks of thrones, alters and obelisks. You’ll want to head to the “Intolerance” Set

blocks.title: “Intolerance” Set
paragraphs: Phelps notices the throne that you’ll have to reach, and also the stairs you’ll need to climb. Jog to the staircase, under the fallen column and the large gates, and climb the stairs. It’s a long way up, but when you get to the top, run through the short corridor and hop onto the wooden platform.

When you land, much of the platform breaks, and the section where you stand is left. Your job is to counterbalance the way that the platform leans with where you stand. So it if leans right, move left. Keep it up until Galloway pushes down a section of wall in front of you, and lean the platform onto the wall to have Phelps automatically jump across.

Walk along the walkway to the first ladder on the left hand side and slide down to the throne platform. Approach the throne, and pick up Evelyn Summer’s Ring and the Seventh Excerpt. Phelps notes that this appears to be the last clue, as it mentions “The place I call home”.

When you have examined both items, the movie set starts to collapse around you. Run through the arch ahead of you, turn right, and sprint down the walkway, hopping down the levels until you reach the ground.
The Excerpt mentions a “Thorn-wounded brow”, tears and a crucifix, which matches the Christ Crown of Thorns, which is a gothic revival church that is now in disrepair. Set that as your destination.

blocks.title: Christ Crown of Thorns
paragraphs: Head into the church to trigger a cutscene where Phelps and Galloway finally confront the man they have been after. After the scene, rush to the alter and trigger another scene, the suspect has fled into the tunnels below the church. Exit via the side door on the right, and it will lead you to a house.

Approach the door to kick it in a quickly scour the area. Head through the kitchen, and kick the door at the back open to reveal the killers “work room”. Inside, you’ll find a number of bloodied apparatus and instruments. When you’ve finished, approach the open shaft and climb down the ladder.

Move carefully through the catacombs, as the killer is trying to gun you down. Poke your head carefully around corners, let the man get off a few shots, then he will retreat to the next corner to wait. Continue to chase him down the corridors until he has no choice but to reveal himself, and then gun him down quickly to end the case, and view the end cutscene.

vehicleOpportunities.note: LA Library parking lot during “The Quarter Moon Murders”

vehicleOpportunities.name: Oldsmobile Hydramatic 88
vehicleOpportunities.note: Parking lot by the Just Picked Fruit Market in “The Silk Stocking Murder”, or the Hall of Records Parking Lot in “The Quarter Moon Murders”

vehicleOpportunities.name: Cadillac V16 Convertible
