vehicleOpportunities.name: Voisin C7
vehicleOpportunities.note: In an Alaco station in Hollywood where Sunset Blvd and La Brea meet. You can also find it in the Hall of Records parking lot during the “Quarter Moon Murders”, and also you drive it in the street crime “Paper Sack Holdup”

cases.title: The Black Caesar
objectives: Use Crane to Gain Access to Ramez Cold Room

blocks.title: Briefing
paragraphs: Your first case for Ad Vice is to investigate two guys who have died after overdosing on Army Surplus Morphine, powerful stuff. Obviously stuff like this needs tracing pretty quickly before it gets too far. You automatically get the army surplus morphine clue, as well as the location of the crime scene added to your book. Fast travel straight there.

blocks.title: Yucca Street Crime Scene
paragraphs: Climb the stairs and follow the walkway around until you find an open doorway, which is the last one on the left. Enter and a scene will trigger, Carruthers is there and gives a quick report. Two overdose victims, Lamont and Tyree, died two days ago from Army Surplus Morphine stolen from a massive robbery at the San Pedro Wharves. Phelps and Earle get their partnership off to a good start and you get to look around the scene.
Start with the guy in the chair. This is Tyrone Lamont, who shows that he has used two syrettes of morphine. Examine his wallet next to him for a positive ID and a numbers slip.

Next, the guy on the floor, Cornell Tyree. Phelps notes that in the marines, one syrette of the stuff was used for combat trauma, and two would stop your heart. Tyree has too many to count. Check his pocket for a wallet, which gives another ID and the radio station note that reads “JJ always listens to 275 FM”. Who is JJ, and why should Tyree need that information?

Next, look at the small table in the lounge. You’ll find some sheet music, as well as the strange doodle clue. Next, pick up the Black Caesar Cup on the table, one of many might I add, and turn it over to see that something was taped to the bottom, but has been removed, which adds popcorn cup to your clues.

Enter the kitchen and find another cup on the counter. Phelps notes that it's heavy for an empty cup. Turn it over and you’ll find what was taped to the bottom of the previous cup, morphine, surprisingly. Your previous clue updates to popcorn cup with morphine, and you also get the morphine syrettes clue. That was probably some expensive popcorn.
Next, you’re going to want to head to the popcorn place at the Black Caesar. The place is only down the road, so it is within walking distance.

blocks.title: The Black Caesar
paragraphs: Approach the store and Earle demands that the man at the counter turn over the popcorn. The guy takes off running, surprisingly, so get after him. You can’t actually catch up to him properly, so just keep up. He leads you over the back wall and climbs a drainpipe to the roof. Eventually, he stops behind a stairwell exit and takes you out with a clothesline. He then calls his friend out for a brawl. Take the guys down and you’ll automatically haul them back to the store for a look around and questioning.

The guy's name is Fleetwood Morgan, and Earle keeps an eye on him for now. Enter the hut and examine the music case in the corner. Examine the trumpet’s mute to open it and find numbers racket slips inside, as well as getting an address for “Ottie’s”. Examine the Blue Room Pass in the case and turn it over to find a name, Jermaine Jones. Finally inspect the cardboard box and open it to find the morphine for distribution. Now it's time to interview Fleetwood.

blocks.title: Fleetwood Morgan

topics.instruction: Morphine Overdose Victims: Accuse - Popcorn cups with morphine
topics.response: Morgan denies that he sold the drugs to Lamont and Tyree, saying he is just a burger flipper. You know he’s flipping way more than that though, so call him with the cups, and he gives up the name of the delivery contact and the boss, Jermaine Jones. This gives you the clue, distributor identified.
Phelps asks about the numbers operation. Morgan gives an angry response, which suggests there’s something you should know. Doubt him and he says that the guy behind the numbers slips is Merlon.

paragraphs: Call in the address for Jones using the phone next to the store, and then head over to the place you’re given.

blocks.title: Jermaine Jones Musical Booking Agency
paragraphs: Climb the stairs and check the directory by the door to find what you’re looking for, office 238. Head inside and follow the hall, entering the first office on the left. Talk to Jermaine Jones, and after some gentle persuasion, he agrees to let you look around his office.

Head for the radio in the corner. Remember what the note you found said? JJ always listens to 275 FM. JJ must be Jones, so turn the VOL dial to switch it on, the BAND dial from AM to FM, and then TUNE it in to 275, and the case opens. Before you get to properly examine it, Jones calls in his goons to take you out.

Knock the guys out and then follow Earle’s advice and check what was in the radio. You find a numbers slip, more morphine syrettes (updates your clue) and a large bag of cannabis. Also, examine the sticker on the underside of the lid, which gives you a new location, Ramez Removals. You’ll need to find out the address though.
Now it's time to chat to Jones.

blocks.title: Jermaine Jones

topics.response: Jones says that he has no idea who it is who supplies the morphine, but that doesn’t really sound that plausible does it? Doubt him, and Jones says he gets his cut, but it is Lenny Finkelstein (Great name by the way), who draws the action. Earle explains that Lenny is head mobster Mickey Cohen’s brother-in-law.

When Phelps connects the numbers slips to the morphine, Jones claims there is no link, and that he doesn’t know anyone called Merlon. Morgan’s statement contradicts this though, so bring it up. Jones admits that Merlon Ottie runs the lottery for “Jew-boy”, and this gives you the Finkelstein Identified clue. Jones says that Ottie is a gambler by nature.

topics.instruction: Link to Ramez Removals: Bad Cop
topics.response: Phelps asks about the removals company, and Jones admits he bought the radio from there. There’s more to it though, so doubt him and Jones says that Ramez is good friends with Lenny the Fink (even better name), which adds him to your list of people to investigate.

paragraphs: Afterwards, a wagon hauls off Jones and his goons. Call in at the game well to get an address for Ramez Removals, and you also get the name of the owner, Jose Ramez. First, let's pay Ottie a visit.

blocks.title: Ottie’s Numbers Operation
paragraphs: Enter the building, and climb the stairs to the second floor to trigger a scene. Merlon Ottie is there, and he claims his operation is legit. Let’s find out shall we?

There is a bank of telephones next to Ottie’s desk, which suggests a possible wire operation. Next, approach the slot machines at the back of the room. Examine the red one, and play in a way that gets you the same pictures as the strange doodle clue you found earlier, in the right order. If you’ve forgot, it's Cherries, Bell, WIN. Keep pulling the lever. And when you get something in the right place, hit the hold button until you have all three right.
This opens a secret compartment, which you’ll find a Ramez Removals sticker again, morphine syrettes and more numbers slips. When you exit the investigation, Merlon takes off running.

Chase him downstairs and across the parking lot. When Ottie goes to the right hand side of the restaurant, cut him off by circling around the left and he will surrender. Once you’ve taken him out one way or another, you’ll take him back to his office.
When you return, Earle hands you Ottie’s cane to have a look at. Examine it, and you’ll find the IOU note, from Jose Ramez to Ottie. Time to interrogate the man.

blocks.title: Merlon Ottie

topics.instruction: Army Surplus Morphine: Accuse - Finkelstein Identified
topics.response: Phelps asks about the morphine. Ottie insists that it isn’t his line of work. You have a statement from Jones though, that proves this lie, so call him on it, and use Finkelstein Identified. Ottie angrily admits that he moves the dope that Ramez brings in, but doesn’t like it.

topics.instruction: IOU Note from Jose Ramez: Good Cop
topics.response: When Phelps asks about the IOU, Ottie admits that “we all owe somebody”. Hard to argue with that, so believe him and he says it's just a gambling debt and has nothing to do with the morphine.

paragraphs: Afterwards, Ottie is hauled off to jail, and you get to head after Ramez.

blocks.title: Ramez Removals
paragraphs: As you get to the removals place, Jose is just leaving in his truck. Get in your car and give chase. Get as close as you can to shoot out the tires. Not long into the chase and the back doors of the truck swing open, and the guy in the back starts chucking stuff out at you. Avoid the debris and continue your chase. When you finally halt the truck, you bring Ramez back to his warehouse. Ramez isn’t saying anything though, so search the warehouse.
Turn left and find the Ramez Removals ledger on the desk. Open it to find a number of deliveries to Merlon Ottie, as well as Polar Bear Ice Company. Hmmm.

On the desk opposite that one is another newspaper (#7) clipping, this time entitled Mickey Cohen. Get the story behind the headlines, and then listen to Earle as he notices a trail of puddles running through the furniture stacks. It leads to a stack of crates next to a room, and the crates are blocking the entrance. Something is clearly in that room.

Find the nearby ladder and climb it. Follow the walkway around to find a mechanism that moves the crane. Use it to lift the boxes and get them out of the way of the door. Now head back down the ladder and enter the cold room.

You’ll find that it is filled with a number of ice blocks, all with something inside. Shoot the block to get the item out, and discover it is a block of morphine syrettes. Take a look at one of the syrettes, and a scene will trigger outside.

A Truck from the Polar Bear Ice Company arrives and starts unloading some ice that you’ve just found. Phelps and Earle arrest the guys, but their lapse of concentration allows Ramez to make a bid for freedom.
Follow Ramez as he loses himself amongst all the furniture. Be wary, he has a shotgun and it not afraid to use it. When you find him, stay in cover until he is visible and then gun him down.
Now, as Phelps puts it, it's time to hunt some polar bear.

blocks.title: Polar Bear Ice Company
paragraphs: Head for the building and a janitor tries to tell you that the factory is closed. Earle is having none of it though, and you bust in. Inside, Finkelstein takes off running, leaving his mini-army to deal with you.

Use the radar to spot red dots that you need to take out before advancing. Try to get as many headshots as possible, as there are quite a few enemies and not only are these one hit kills, but you can rack up quite a few kills to your headshot total.

Fight your way across the loading bay into the bar area. Be aware of the guy in the window behind the bar. Continue down the hallway and into the machine room. Fight your way around the pumping machine in the middle of the room, and head for the cool room, which has more ice blocks filled with morphine. Fight through the first floor, up the stairs, and a scene triggers.

Phelps and Earle hold Finkelstein at gunpoint, but he refuses to go down quietly. When the scene ends, put a bullet in him, and then end the case by examining the USS Coolridge crates that Earle heads to.
